title: Best Real-Time Sales Coaching Software in 2026
summary: Compare the best real-time sales coaching software in 2026: Clari Copilot, Dialpad, Outreach Kaia, Nooks and Caretta, plus where Gong and Avoma fit.
body_markdown:
The best real-time sales coaching software closes the gap between your best rep and everyone else while the call is still happening, instead of in a review three days later. This guide compares the live coaching tools worth buying in 2026, and is honest about which problems each one does and does not solve.


## 01


What is real-time sales coaching software?


Real-time sales coaching software listens to a live sales call and guides the rep during it: answering the hard question, countering the objection, or nudging them back on track before the moment passes. The point is a manager's problem, and an old one. Your top rep handles the pricing ambush without blinking. Your newest rep freezes, says "let me get back to you", and the deal cools. You cannot sit on every call, so the software has to carry your best answers into the calls you will never hear.


Before comparing tools, separate three things that all get sold as "coaching":


- **Live coaching** : help during real calls with real buyers. This is the subject of this post.
- **Roleplay coaching** : practice against an AI buyer before real calls. Hyperbound leads here. Good for ramping and drills; useless once a real prospect is talking.
- **Post-call coaching** : review after the call, from recordings and scorecards. Gong and Avoma own this ground. Good for patterns and skill development; too late for the deal on the line today.


Buying the wrong category is the most common mistake in this market. A team drowning in lost deals needs live help; a team with a ramp problem may need roleplay first.


## 02


How do the live coaching tools compare?


Tool How it coaches live Best for Watch out for


Caretta Listens to the call and answers questions and objections using your docs, CRM, and past calls Teams that want every rep answering like the top rep Focused on meetings; not a dialler


Clari Copilot Keyword-triggered battlecards and monologue alerts Teams already on Clari for forecasting Cards need manual building and keyword tuning


Dialpad Ai Real-time assist cards inside Dialpad's phone system Teams using Dialpad as their phone and contact centre Tied to Dialpad telephony; keyword-driven cards


Outreach Kaia Live content cards and capture inside Outreach meetings Outreach-centred sales orgs Needs the Outreach platform; setup effort

## 03


The best real-time sales coaching tools in 2026


### 1. Caretta


Built on the coaching premise directly: your organisation already knows the answer to almost every hard question a prospect asks, but that knowledge lives in your top reps' heads, your docs, your CRM, and hundreds of past calls. The copilot learns from all of it, then joins live calls and surfaces the right answer or objection response at the moment the rep is stuck. Because guidance comes from your own material rather than hand-built keyword cards, there is no battlecard library to maintain, and the help stays specific to your product and your deals. It also briefs reps before meetings and handles follow-up after, so coaching covers the whole call cycle. You can see how the live guidance works on the[product page](https://www.caretta.so/product) . The honest limit: it is built for scheduled meetings and conversations, so a pure cold-calling floor that lives in a dialler will want a dialler-native tool alongside it.


### 2. Clari Copilot


Clari Copilot (formerly Wingman) pops battlecards when trigger words come up, warns reps who monologue too long, and lets managers join calls live. Its real pull is the platform: if your organisation already runs forecasting on Clari, coaching data and revenue data sit together, and RevOps will like that. The tradeoff is the card model. Someone has to write the battlecards, pick the trigger keywords, and keep both current, and keyword triggers misfire in both directions: firing on innocent mentions and missing objections phrased in new words. It coaches well on the objections you predicted, less well on the ones you did not.


### 3. Dialpad Ai


Dialpad bakes coaching into its phone system. Real-time assist cards appear when set phrases come up, live transcription runs in the call, and supervisors can monitor and whisper from the contact-centre side. If Dialpad is already your phone, this is coaching you nearly get for free, and that is a genuinely strong position. If it is not your phone, the calculus flips: you would be replacing your telephony to get the coaching layer, which is a much bigger decision than buying a coaching tool. The cards share the keyword-trigger weakness above, and the coaching depth reflects its contact-centre roots more than complex B2B selling.


### 4. Outreach Kaia


Kaia is Outreach's meeting assistant: it joins calls booked through Outreach, transcribes live, and surfaces content cards your enablement team has loaded when relevant topics come up. For orgs that run their whole motion in Outreach, it keeps coaching inside the tool reps already live in, and the captured answers flow back into the platform. The dependency is also the limit. Kaia makes little sense outside an Outreach contract, and like Clari it coaches from prepared cards, so the quality of live help equals the quality and freshness of what enablement built.


### 5. Nooks


Nooks approaches live coaching from the SDR floor. It is a parallel dialler with a virtual sales floor: managers hear calls as they happen, whisper guidance mid-call, and the team works in one room again, even remote. AI features score calls and assist, but the coaching heart is human and immediate, which many SDR leaders find is what actually changes cold-call behaviour. Judge it for what it is: a tool for high-volume outbound dialling. It will not coach a 45-minute discovery call or a demo, and it is not trying to.


## 04


Where do Gong and Avoma fit?


Gong and Avoma are coaching tools, but post-call ones. Gong records and analyses conversations at scale, flags risk in deals, and gives managers scorecards and clip libraries to coach from. Avoma does meeting notes and coaching dashboards at a friendlier price. Both make your coaching reviews sharper. Neither helps the rep at the moment the prospect says "your competitor is half the price". That gap is why teams that already own Gong still add a live layer; we cover that pairing in[Gong alternatives for real-time coaching](https://www.caretta.so/blog/gong-alternatives-real-time-coaching) . If your managers never review calls at all, though, start post-call: live coaching works best when someone is also watching the patterns.


## 05


Which tool should you pick?


Match the tool to where your deals die. If they die on cold calls, Nooks. If they die in meetings because reps cannot answer hard questions, pick a tool that draws on your organisation's real knowledge rather than a card library you must maintain. If you are already deep in Clari, Dialpad, or Outreach, their native options are credible and cheap to adopt, with the keyword-card ceiling described above. And if reps fail in ways practice would fix, buy roleplay before any of this.
